name: Early Blight
summary: A fungal disease (Alternaria) that starts on older, lower leaves and spreads upward.
symptoms: Brown spots with rings like a target on older leaves
Yellowing around the spots
Lower leaves dry and drop
causes: Spores splash from soil and old plant debris
Warm, humid weather with leaf wetness
treatment: Remove and destroy badly affected leaves
Spray a recommended fungicide (e.g. mancozeb or chlorothalonil) following label rates
Repeat sprays every 7–10 days during wet weather
prevention: Rotate away from tomato, pepper and garden egg for 2–3 years
Mulch to stop soil splashing onto leaves
Stake plants and space them for airflow
Water at the base, not over leaves
monitoring: Check lower leaves twice a week
Rescan in 7 days to see if spots are spreading

name: Late Blight
summary: A fast-spreading water mould disease that can destroy a tomato field within days in cool, wet weather.
symptoms: Large greasy, dark patches on leaves
White fuzzy growth under leaves in humid mornings
Brown, firm rot on fruit
causes: Spores carried by wind and rain
Cool nights with long leaf wetness
treatment: Remove and bury or burn infected plants immediately
Spray a systemic fungicide (e.g. metalaxyl + mancozeb) following label rates
Warn neighbouring farms — it spreads by wind
prevention: Plant in the dry season where possible
monitoring: Inspect daily during cool, rainy spells
Rescan in 3 days

name: Bacterial Spot
summary: A bacterial disease causing small dark spots on leaves and scabby spots on fruit.
symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked spots on leaves
Spots may have a yellow halo
Raised, scabby spots on fruit
causes: Rain splash and handling wet plants
treatment: Remove badly affected leaves
Copper-based bactericide sprays can slow spread
Avoid working in the field when plants are wet
monitoring: Check new leaves after each rain
Rescan in 7 days

name: Septoria Leaf Spot
summary: A fungal leaf spot that causes many small round spots and early leaf loss.
symptoms: Many small round spots with grey centres and dark edges
Tiny black dots inside the spots
Lower leaves yellow and fall
treatment: Remove affected lower leaves
Spray a recommended fungicide (e.g. chlorothalonil or mancozeb)
prevention: Clear and destroy crop debris after harvest
Mulch and water at the base
monitoring: Rescan in 7 days

name: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
summary: A virus spread by whiteflies that stunts plants and sharply reduces fruit set.
symptoms: Leaves curl upward and become small and yellow at the edges
Plants are stunted and bushy
Flowers drop; few fruits
treatment: There is no cure — uproot and destroy infected plants early
Control whiteflies with recommended insecticides or neem extract
Use yellow sticky traps
monitoring: Check undersides of leaves for whiteflies
Rescan new plants weekly
conditions: Hot, dry season with high whitefly numbers

name: Healthy Tomato
summary: No disease detected on this tomato leaf.
prevention: Maintain good spacing, staking and mulching
monitoring: Rescan if you see new spots, curling or yellowing

name: Northern Leaf Blight
summary: A fungal disease producing long, cigar-shaped grey-brown lesions on maize leaves.
symptoms: Long (2–15 cm) cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions
Lesions start on lower leaves
Severe cases dry out whole leaves before grain fill
treatment: Fungicide is worthwhile only if lesions reach the ear leaf before tasselling
Follow label rates of a recommended triazole or strobilurin
monitoring: Check the ear leaf around tasselling
Rescan in 10 days

name: Common Rust
summary: A fungal disease producing rusty brown powdery pustules on both sides of maize leaves.
symptoms: Small, raised, brick-red to brown pustules
Powdery spores rub off on fingers
Pustules on both leaf surfaces
treatment: Usually no spray needed on tolerant varieties
On susceptible varieties with early heavy infection, use a recommended fungicide
monitoring: Rescan in 10 days
conditions: Highlands such as the Jos Plateau

name: Gray Leaf Spot
summary: A fungal disease producing narrow, rectangular grey lesions limited by leaf veins.
symptoms: Rectangular tan to grey lesions running parallel to veins
Lesions merge and kill leaves
treatment: Use a recommended fungicide if lesions spread up the plant before silking
monitoring: Rescan in 10 days

name: Maize Streak Virus
summary: A leafhopper-spread virus causing broken yellow streaks along maize leaves.
symptoms: Narrow broken yellow-white streaks along leaf veins
Stunted plants when infected young
Poorly filled cobs
causes: Maize streak virus spread by Cicadulina leafhoppers
treatment: There is no cure — uproot badly stunted young plants
prevention: Plant early and at the same time as neighbours
monitoring: Check seedlings in the first 4 weeks
conditions: Dry spells early in the season

name: Healthy Maize
summary: No disease detected on this maize leaf.
prevention: Scout for fall armyworm in the leaf funnel weekly
monitoring: Rescan if you see spots, streaks or holes

name: Cassava Mosaic Disease
summary: A whitefly-spread virus disease, the most damaging cassava disease in Nigeria.
symptoms: Yellow and green mosaic pattern on leaves
Leaves twisted and reduced in size
Stunted plants with small roots
treatment: There is no cure — uproot and destroy infected plants early (roguing)
Do not take cuttings from infected plants
prevention: Use clean cuttings from healthy fields
monitoring: Check young plants 1–3 months after planting

name: Cassava Brown Streak Disease
summary: A virus disease that causes leaf yellowing and dry brown rot inside the roots.
symptoms: Yellow patches along secondary leaf veins
Brown streaks on green stems
Dry, brown, corky rot inside roots
treatment: Uproot and destroy infected plants
Harvest early if roots are still usable
prevention: Report suspected cases to extension officers — it is a quarantine concern in West Africa
monitoring: Cut a root open at harvest to check for brown rot

name: Cassava Bacterial Blight
summary: A bacterial disease causing angular leaf spots, wilting and stem dieback.
symptoms: Angular, water-soaked leaf spots
Leaves wilt and fall
Gum ooze and dieback from stem tips
treatment: Cut out and burn affected shoots
Disinfect cutting tools
monitoring: Rescan after heavy rains

name: Healthy Cassava
summary: No disease detected on this cassava leaf.
prevention: Keep using clean cuttings and resistant varieties
monitoring: Rescan if you see mosaic patterns or leaf twisting

name: Bacterial Spot
summary: A bacterial disease that spots leaves and fruit and causes leaf drop.
symptoms: Small water-soaked spots that turn brown
Yellowing leaves that drop
Raised scabby spots on fruit
treatment: Remove badly affected leaves
Copper-based sprays can slow spread
prevention: Rotate crops away from tomato and pepper
monitoring: Rescan in 7 days

name: Healthy Pepper
summary: No disease detected on this pepper leaf.
prevention: Watch for aphids and thrips under leaves
monitoring: Rescan if you see spots or curling
